mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.22 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns during inflation spikes are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not exceed 0.22 for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the expected discount rate on future cash flows increases, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During identified tightening episodes, 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median < 0 but 90% CI includes zero), or FEDFUNDS change is ≤0.25% in all trigger months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressure that outpaces productivity, increasing labor costs for firms and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >0.5% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During wage pressure periods, 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1), or PAYEMS growth ≤0.5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in RSAFS retail sales exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces future earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >2% in the current month
failure_condition: During confirmed demand shocks, 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1), or RSAFS decline is ≤1% in all identified shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in INDPRO manufacturing index below 100 (after normalization) suggests supply-side constraints, raising uncertainty and pushing up equity risk premia, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 in the current month
failure_condition: During supply shocks, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1), or INDPRO recovers to ≥100 within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly declines in HOUST housing starts and GDPC1 personal consumption both exceeding 1% suggest dual demand pressures, amplifying equity market volatility and producing positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST and GDPC1 fall by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: During dual-demand weakness, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (median ≤ 0, 90% CI includes zero), or either proxy recovers within 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months during a labor market recovery, the reduced labor market friction lowers the cost of hiring and boosts corporate earnings expectations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During easing episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1), or UNRATE remains ≥3.0% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS below 4.0% in a holding pattern signals a prolonged easing stance, which lowers real rates and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During prolonged easing, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (median ≤ 0, 90% CI includes zero), or FEDFUNDS re-enters ≥4.0% within 2 months.
